notes: Which policy governs (V3c): the university-wide Family Leave for New Parents policy (2018_00_link, effective July 1, 2017) and the Homewood Schools FML policy (2018_02, undated, pre-dates July 2017 and does not mention the university policy) both cover Homewood tenure-stream faculty and differ (8 weeks paid maternity leave vs 6 weeks birth recovery; Homewood unpaid parental leave vs 4 weeks paid parental leave; Homewood teaching relief has no university counterpart). The university-wide policy sets the figures; every 2018_02 provision is recorded with faculty_group naming the Homewood group and faculty_scope set, as in the V3c Johns Hopkins example. The Homewood Tenure Regulations (2018_01) have no university-wide counterpart among the saved documents, so their tenure-clock provisions are coded main_campus_tenure_stream with faculty_scope Homewood (V3, V3b).

Version: 2018_02 carries no date; its version note places it in force from at least March 2017 to January 2021 (copy captured 2020-11-25). 2018_01 is headed 'Effective October 15, 2016' (copy captured 2024). 2018_00_link is the Wayback capture of 2018-01-02, effective July 1, 2017.
The Tenure Regulations cite the 'Family and Medical Leave Act Guidelines' for the Homewood Schools; per the version note this is the Homewood FML policy (2018_02), so it is treated as saved.

Documents cited but not saved: Johns Hopkins University Family and Medical Leave Policy; Johns Hopkins University Sick Leave Policy; Faculty Parental Leave Guidelines; Johns Hopkins University Adoption Assistance Policy; Policy Regarding Reasonable Break Time for Nursing Mothers; Breastfeeding Support Program; Human Resources Policy section 6 (full-time and part-time employment); New Child Accommodations for Full-Time Graduate Students and Postdoctoral Trainees Policy (other group); Benefits website pages for Birth Recovery Leave and Parental Leave; Appointment and Promotion Procedures for Tenure Track Faculty. Forms (Request for Leave, Parental Leave Request Form, Adoption Assistance Form, Breastfeeding Support Program Registration Form, Faculty and Staff Request for Reasonable Workplace Accommodation Form) are not policies. The Adoption Assistance Policy is financial assistance, not leave; the workplace accommodation form concerns disability accommodation (not a component).

Exclusions in 2018_00_link: limited and casual faculty and staff; interns, residents and postdoctoral trainees; Applied Physics Laboratory employees; Johns Hopkins Emergency Medical Services. 2018_02 excludes Postdoctoral Fellows. None excludes main-campus tenure-stream faculty.
Pay prorated for part-time schedules under 2018_00_link (e.g., 32 hours/week: 192 hours birth recovery, 128 hours parental); the member described (full-time) receives the full 6 and 4 weeks.

Homewood research faculty: pay for leave from grants 'if the funding agency allows', otherwise from the faculty member's discretionary funds; 'a maximum of 8 weeks per effort reporting period can be charged to any sponsored funds'; ill-family leave paid only if supporting grants cover it. Recorded in notes and on c6's flags; no separate components (no employer guarantee).

Homewood: 'Health, dental, life, and disability insurance benefits remain in effect during leaves, provided the faculty member pays his/her portion' (benefit continuation, not a component). 'Military Leave of Absence will be unpaid' (not usable for a birth; not a component). Administration: where the policy conflicts with the FMLA, the more favorable application takes precedence.

Chain, birth parent: Birth Recovery Leave 6 (to 13 on medical necessity; STD within it from week 2, employee-paid) -> Parental Leave 4; FMLA 12 alongside from the birth (S1). Homewood (not counted): Maternity/Medical Leave 8 (to 90 days) within FMLA and concurrent with Birth Recovery Leave; Teaching Relief one semester also_available with it; FML extension after FMLA.
Chain, non-birth parent: Parental Leave 4, with FMLA 12 alongside from the birth (S1). Homewood (not counted): Teaching Relief one semester; FML extension after FMLA.

statutory_floor.statute: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) (29 U.S.C. 2611-2612)
